ai.description: This large turtle reaches 90 cm in shell length. It features a dark olive to blackish leathery carapace and a greyish head with a tubular snout. It is distinguished by its lack of marginal scutes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Nilssonia nigricans* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark-colored patch or "ocellus" pattern on its carapace, which fades into a uniform blackish hue.
ai.habitat: The Black Softshell Turtle inhabits freshwater ponds and temple tanks in the Brahmaputra River basin, typically at low altitudes with dense aquatic vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Black Softshell Turtle is primarily crepuscular, often emerging at dawn and dusk to forage for aquatic plants, mollusks, and small fish in its freshwater habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nilssonia nigricans* is oviparous, laying clutches of 15–38 eggs. Breeding typically occurs from February to May in its native range in Assam, India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Black Softshell Turtle is primarily found in the Brahmaputra River basin in Assam, India, and parts of the Sylhet division in Bangladesh.
